claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Thanks for your help. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex, who's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! Thanks for getting in touch. I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you a few questions to assess your eligibility.

Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

Now, could you tell me about your living arrangements with Alex? Does he live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Lovely, thank you for that information.

Just a couple more questions to confirm your eligibility:

Is Alex currently in any form of local authority care, hospital, or residential accommodation? Or does he live with you full-time at home?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex has been in hospital for a while now - a few months. He had a serious health issue that required extended treatment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to hear that Alex has been unwell. I hope he's making good progress with his treatment.

Thank you for letting me know about this. Since Alex has been in hospital for a few months, I need to ask a bit more about the situation, as this can affect Child Benefit eligibility.

Could you tell me approximately how long Alex has been in hospital? Specifically, has it been more than 12 weeks?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, it hasn't been quite that long - it's been about 11 weeks now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I'm glad to hear it hasn't reached the 12-week mark yet.

Just one more question regarding this: While Alex has been in hospital, have you been regularly spending money on him? This could include things like buying him clothes, toys, treats, or other items for his comfort and care.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have. I still buy his clothes, magazines, and favorite food to bring to him at the hospital.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's really thoughtful of you, and it's also helpful information for your Child Benefit eligibility.

One final question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- You live in the UK
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- He normally lives with you
- He has been in hospital for about 11 weeks (which is under the 12-week limit)
- You continue to regularly spend money on him while he's in hospital
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

I'm pleased to let you know that you should be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of the key reasons:

- ✅ You live in the UK
- ✅ Alex is under 16 years old
- ✅ Alex normally lives with you, so you're responsible for him
- ✅ Although Alex has been in hospital for about 11 weeks, this is under the 12-week threshold that can affect Child Benefit
- ✅ You continue to regularly spend money on Alex while he's in hospital (clothes, magazines, food)
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

**Important things to note:**

1. If Alex's hospital stay extends beyond 12 weeks, you should inform HMRC. However, because you're regularly spending money on him, you may still remain eligible even after the 12-week period.

2. If Alex leaves hospital but then goes back within 28 days, the total time spent in hospital will count towards the 12-week limit.

I hope Alex recovers well and comes home soon. Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
